summary: Shigeru Matsumoto (1933–2010) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1962) and Harvard University (~1962–1967). He taught at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1969–1999) and Tenri University (~1999–2004).

Shigetsu Sasaki (1882–1945) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts (~1901–1905) and under Sokatsu Shaku (~1905–1921). He founded the First Zen Institute of America in 1931.
Shili Xiong (1885–1968) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the China Inner Learning College in 1920. He held a post at Peking University from 1923 to 1955.

Shin Fujinaga (b. 1958) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held positions at Hiroshima University (attested 1992) and as an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested 1998–2000).
Shin Kitada is an Indologist who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held a post at the Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu (1889–1980) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida (~1915–1918) and Shozan Ikegami, later teaching at Kyoto University, Ryukoku University, Hanazono University, and Harvard.

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga (1957–2022) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1975–1980) and held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College (~1991–2018).

Shindai Sekiguchi (1907–1986) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1927–1931). He served as a professor at Taisho University (~1957–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1984).

Shingen Takagi (b. 1932) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, and others. He served at Koyasan University as associate professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995).

Shingo Einoo (b. 1948) is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1981–1986) under Wilhelm Rau. He served as a research assistant at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1988–1989).

Shinichi Tsuda (b. 1938) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at Australian National University under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham, later teaching at the Eastern Institute and ICPBS.

Shinjo Hinonishi (1928–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He served at Koyasan University as an associate professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

Shinjo Kawasaki (b. 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. After studying at Columbia University and under Hajime Nakamura and others, he held positions at Toyo Bunko, the University at Buffalo, University of Tsukuba, and Taisho University.

Shinjo Suguro (1925–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948, Lit.D. 1987). He served as deputy director and later professor emeritus at Rissho University.
Shinkai Sugawara (1925–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1946–1951) and later held an academic post there (~1971–1996).

Shinkan Murakami (b. 1932) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed his doctoral studies at Tohoku University. He served as professor at Tohoku University and later taught at Seiwa Gakuen College (~1996–2003).

Shinko Mochizuki (1869–1948) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University. He served as president of Shukyo University (1914–1928) and Taisho University (1930–1932), alongside professorial and leadership roles at Taisho (~1926–1942).

Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under Mark Csikszentmihalyi (2000), academic adviser Robert Bickner, and doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003).
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Nagoya University in 1995. She held a post as professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Shinsho Hanayama (1898–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1959) and held posts at Kokugakuin University and Toyo University (~1959).
